rv.q: This is British theatre operating at the very top of its game.
Hollander is pompous and preening in this essential revival which has transferred to the West End from the Menier Chocolate Factory.
The wit and larky intellectualism on display in Tom Stoppard’s 1974 play will have you smirking with pleasure.
My expectations ran high at the prospect of Travesties, and it does not disappoint.

Equal part bonkers and fabulous it's like a Rubik's cube for the mind - with each turn you find yourself closer to the solution yet further away from the centre, and that's the joy of Stoppard's idiosyncrasy.
What Patrick Marber has done in directing this revival...is make it more accessible by slowing it down...But in the process, for me, he has lost some of that runaway horse quality.
I felt alienated through out by how smugly pleased with itself the play is.

But together with textual revisions making this a newly-definitive production, with the cast re-moulding it and above all Hollander’s superbly faltering diffidence, this is the outstanding revival of a play in the West End this season.
Stoppard's dazzling intellectual and verbal jeu d'esprit is carried off by Tom Hollander and Freddie Fox, who play Henry Carr and Tristan Tzara respectively, with panache.

cn.t: Stoppard's dazzling verbal fireworks and intellectual wit largely captivate in this well-received revival, though some find the chaotic wordplay bewildering. Hollander impresses in Marber's production.
